title: Terminal-Universe: Turning Agent Trajectories into Scalable Terminal Environments
authors: Jie Wu, Zhenru Zhang (project leader), Beichen Zhang, Xuwu Wang, Yuhui Su, Mouxiang Chen, Peng Wang, Zhihai Wang, Que Shen, Hao Zhou, An Yang, Fei Huang, Yujiu Yang, Dayiheng Liu (corresponding authors Yujiu Yang and Dayiheng Liu)
lab: Qwen Team, Alibaba Group, and Tsinghua University (Jie Wu worked on it as a Qwen intern)
date: 3 September 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version so far)

code.title: no code or data released
code.note: The paper links no code, no environments, no SFT corpus and no model (checked in the arXiv HTML and LaTeX source, 3 October 2026). What is public are its source trajectories; the largest, LFM2-Terminal-SFT-Processed (139,841 trajectories, the count in Table 12), is the one this page replays. About 10 minutes to browse a few rows in the dataset viewer

takeaway: Agent trajectories already contain their own environments, because the file operations they recorded can be replayed: rebuild the workspace from the log, fill missing dependencies, then grow tasks by breadth (cross-workspace queries) and depth (single-turn extended into multi-round with feedback), yielding 37,300 runnable environments from public traces; fine-tuning Qwen3.5-27B gives +11.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and +13.8 on EvoCode-Bench v2 MT@4, and closes an agents-to-trajectories-to-environments-to-agents flywheel.
verdict: Believe the core move: re-solving rebuilt environments with a strong teacher clearly beats imitating the original traces (52.1 against 36.7, far outside the noise), and the headline gains over the base model are real. Treat the rest as provisional: most component ablations differ by 0.4 to 2.8 points, within about two standard errors of run-to-run noise; the gains are distillation from Qwen3.7-Max as much as a property of the environments; the comparison table mixes base models, scaffolds and reported numbers; and an "environment" here is a mostly model-written workspace that an LLM judged sufficient, not one checked to run.

resources.t: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
resources.by: Merrill, Shaw, Carlini et al., ICLR 2026
resources.n: The benchmark the headline is measured on; what an expert-built environment (container, instruction, verifier) looks like, which this paper tries to manufacture at scale.
Shows Terminal-Bench 4.0 as the current version (checked 3 October 2026); the paper reports 2.0 and 2.1, so its numbers are not comparable with current model cards.
The paper's footnote for how 2.1 differs from 2.0.

resources.t: EvoCode-Bench: Evaluating Coding Agents in Multi-Turn Iterative Interactions
resources.n: The multi-round benchmark behind MT@4 and the Case score: 26 tasks, 227 rounds, persistent workspaces, cumulative verifiers.
The source of 96% of the sufficient terminal environments. Every row this page sampled is a Terminus-2 rollout by DeepSeek-V3.2 on a generated task; open a row to see what a "trajectory" is here.

resources.t: Training frontier knowledge-work agents: a 397B RL training guide with SkyRL
resources.by: Mercor and SkyRL, filed in this knowledge base on 7 September 2026
resources.n: The practitioner side: argues that environment robustness and harness design decide an RL run as much as the algorithm, which is the input this paper industrialises.

kb.t: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
kb.n: The complement: wraps existing frozen environments with composable Stage, Contract and Chain components and customises them against a policy's diagnosed weaknesses; Terminal-Universe manufactures new environments from artifacts nobody treated as environments. Together they cover supply and adaptation.

kb.t: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills
kb.n: The same week, the same move applied to skills instead of environments: both mine artifacts that already exist.

kb.t: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
kb.n: A harness-building model needs somewhere to practise; this is that somewhere.

kb.t: StateM: Reaching 95.3% Raw Accuracy, or a $15 Frontier Run, on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via Harness Scaling
kb.n: The same benchmark version from the harness side: how much of a Terminal-Bench 2.1 score the scaffold, not the model, can move.

kb.t: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work - Until They Don't
kb.n: Another way to reuse recorded trajectories: distil them into skills at run time instead of rebuilding environments for training.

kb.t: Schrödinger's Code Repository: Have LLMs Learned SWE-bench or Memorized It?
kb.n: Why the decontamination step matters: benchmark repositories leak into training data. Terminal-Universe filters Terminal-Bench sources and SWE-bench Verified repositories.
The model family whose later members (Qwen3.5-27B, Qwen3.7-Max) are the student and the teacher here.

kb.t: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
kb.n: Where the trajectory format comes from: interleaved reasoning, actions and observations, which is exactly what replay mines.

topics.n: Harness-scaling section: environments are the input that harness and post-training work both consume.
For the post-training use. The paper itself only does SFT; its verified environments are RL-ready in principle, untested.
Distillation from a stronger teacher as a post-training recipe.
Terminal-Bench versions and EvoCode-Bench; the reported gains are on Terminal-Bench 2.1, not the current 4.0.

takeaway_note: The database Takeaway, verbatim. Two corrections from the paper: the 37,300 (37,273) environments are judged task-sufficient by an LLM, not shown runnable, and 1,464 of them are SWE repositories outside the main corpus; and the flywheel is the idea, not what the paper ran (its sources are mostly one model's rollouts on generated tasks).
